import pandas as pd

# Load source tables with index_col=0 to ignore the numerical index column
source0 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/intermediate_space/length3_24/training_0.csv", index_col=0)
source1 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/intermediate_space/length3_24/training_1.csv", index_col=0)
source2 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/intermediate_space/length3_24/training_2.csv", index_col=0)

# Step 1: Join Source1 and Source2 on movie_id
join_1 = pd.merge(source1, source2, on="movie_id", how="inner")

# Step 2: Join the result with Source0 on user_id
join_2 = pd.merge(join_1, source0, on="user_id", how="inner")

# Step 3: Compute average ratings by gender for each title
# Filter ratings by gender and group by title
# Pivot to get columns 'F' and 'M' with average ratings

# Group by title and gender, calculate mean rating
grouped = join_2.groupby(['title', 'gender'])['rating'].mean().reset_index()

# Pivot to have genders as columns
pivot = grouped.pivot(index='title', columns='gender', values='rating').reset_index()

# Rename columns to match target schema
pivot = pivot.rename(columns={'F': 'F', 'M': 'M'})

# Ensure columns order and types
pivot = pivot[['title', 'F', 'M']]

# Convert 'title' to string, 'F' and 'M' to float
pivot['title'] = pivot['title'].astype(str)
pivot['F'] = pivot['F'].astype(float)
pivot['M'] = pivot['M'].astype(float)

# Save the final target table
pivot.to_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length3_24/target_multisource.csv", index=False)

import pandas as pd

# Read source tables with index_col=0 to ignore the numerical index column
source0 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length3_24/training_0.csv", index_col=0)
source1 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length3_24/training_1.csv", index_col=0)
source2 = pd.read_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length3_24/training_2.csv", index_col=0)

# Join Source1 and Source2 on movie_id
joined_1_2 = pd.merge(source1, source2, on="movie_id", how="inner")

# Join Source0 and the above join on user_id
joined_all = pd.merge(source0, joined_1_2, on="user_id", how="inner")

# Create separate columns for F and M ratings by gender
joined_all["F"] = joined_all.apply(lambda row: row["rating"] if row["gender"] == "F" else None, axis=1)
joined_all["M"] = joined_all.apply(lambda row: row["rating"] if row["gender"] == "M" else None, axis=1)

# Group by title and aggregate mean of F and M ratings
result = joined_all.groupby("title", as_index=False).agg({"F": "mean", "M": "mean"})

# Write the result to the target CSV file
result.to_csv("autopipeline-benchmarks/github-pipelines/length3_24/target_multisource_critique_history.csv", index=False)
